attrs.evidence: lowering_check.mjs: lowering-is-deterministic (the same AST lowers to the same string twice, and the RELATION id is separate from the APPLICATION receipt), re-lowering-verifies (lowering again independently reaches the same target_term_sem_id, and add(3,2) reaches a different one so the id is not vacuous), out-of-fragment-refused (input, read, sub, a non-integer constant and a negative constant are each a NAMED refusal). native-execution-observed cross-checks the target term's identity against the C side: the kernel's target_term_sem_id equals ic32_canon's canonical id for the same lowered term, so both planes agree on what was fed in before either says what came out. B1.2.1 adds emit-is-not-a-hidden-relation (three emitter mutations move the instantiation id and not lowering's; two per-op rule mutations move lowering's and not instantiation's; a template-grammar mutation moves both and the template-encoding id; every name in refusal_semantics is driven to a refusal) and chain-identities-stay-distinct, whose set is DERIVED from REFINEMENT_CHAIN rather than hand-typed. B2: lower() interprets op_lowering_rules; lowering_check migration-preserves-the-old-bytes and implementing-moved-neither-id.
attrs.revision_note: SUPERSEDED at B2.1 and kept as history. Revision 3 described instantiation as a single relation that both substituted and emitted, and permitted a rule vocabulary of bare names. NO FALSE VERDICT WAS ACCEPTED BY THE ASSURANCE MACHINERY -- but revision 3 did permit a real compiler-layer defect, the two-read input binding, which is recorded in the successor rather than here because the successor is where it is fixed.
attrs.statement: ONE SOURCE PROGRAM UNDER ONE LOWERING SEMANTICS DETERMINES ONE CANONICAL TARGET TERM. lowering_sem_id identifies the lowering SEMANTICS — H over the LOWERING SEMANTICS alone: the source core_sem_id, the id of its CODOMAIN encoding (TRVM-TARGET-TEMPLATE-v1, and NOT the executable encoding, which is instantiation's codomain), the per-op lowering map, the refusal vocabulary lower() can actually produce, and totality on the fragment — and is a different object from a record of what happened when a particular program was lowered, which is a LoweringReceipt {program_sem_id, lowering_sem_id, target_template_sem_id}. One id must not silently answer both 'which lowering semantics is this?' and 'what did lowering do here?'. THE INSTRUMENT IS RE-LOWERING, NOT A FILM. A semantic film is evidence for a TRANSITION SYSTEM; lowering is a relation DeriveProgram -> TargetTerm. Filming it would invent a sequence of internal compiler steps and make implementation strategy semantic — the mistake the read-order ruling refused when it kept access order out of the footprint. Verification is: re-lower the program independently under lowering_sem_id, canonicalise, and require target_term_sem_id to agree. DECIDED AT B1 AND BUILT AT B1.2, and the earlier framing was wrong: whether lowering is PARAMETERIZED (program -> target term with input ports, so target_term_sem_id is a function of the program alone) or INSTANTIATED (program + canonical_inputs -> closed target term) was a FALSE CHOICE. The template is parameterized AND the executed term is necessarily closed, so there are TWO relations with two identities and lowering's codomain is the TEMPLATE. This statement said DEFERRED for three passes after the decision, and printed the pre-B1.2 receipt shape for one -- while grid_check REQUIRED the deferred wording, which turns a check into a ratchet holding a stale record in place. See derivation.instantiation-identity@3. CORRECTED AT B1.2.1, AND emit() WAS A HIDDEN SEMANTIC RELATION. B1.2 moved lowering's codomain onto the template and left BOTH encoding commitments pointing where they had pointed when there was no template. MEASURED: change the add combinator and nothing else, and the executable term's bytes change while INSTANTIATION_SEM_ID, target_template_sem_id and the template-encoding id all stand still -- so the identity of the relation that PRODUCES those bytes did not move. LOWERING_SEM_ID moved instead, which is the same mistake facing the other way. UNDER-BOUND: INSTANTIATION_SEMANTICS named its codomain in PROSE, 'TRVM-TERM-CANON-v1 / ic32 executable text, via emit()', so the whole executable encoding reached the relation's identity only as a symbol name inside an English sentence -- a label anyone may claim, the objection the primitive ruling already raised against a bare componentReachability. OVER-BOUND: LOWERING_SEMANTICS still carried the entire TARGET_ENCODING, a pre-template leftover of the same class as the LoweringReceipt that kept ending at target_term_sem_id, which B1.2 fixed one declaration away and missed here; an emitter change therefore re-identified every LoweringReceipt ever issued, for a relation lowering does not perform. THE RULE: A RELATION'S IDENTITY MUST COMMIT, BY CONTENT AND NOT BY NAME, TO EXACTLY THE ENCODINGS OF ITS OWN DOMAIN AND CODOMAIN -- no more and no fewer. Lowering commits to TRVM-TARGET-TEMPLATE-v1 and to its own per-op map; instantiation commits to the template encoding as domain and to TARGET_EXECUTABLE_ENCODING_SEM_ID as codomain, and EMISSION IS INSIDE THE INSTANTIATION RELATION. That last is a ruling with a stated trigger for revisiting it rather than a convenience: a third relation with its own emission_sem_id is the more faithful decomposition, because a correct port substitution can coexist with an incorrect emitter, and it is NOT taken while emit() is neither independently reused nor independently theorem-bearing. MEASURED IN THREE DIRECTIONS: an emitter change moves the instantiation id ALONE, a per-op lowering-rule change moves lowering's ALONE, and a template-grammar change moves BOTH because it is the boundary they share. REMOVING THE LEFTOVER BINDING EXPOSED A SECOND GAP: nothing in the hashed lowering semantics said that a const becomes a church node or that add's operand order is preserved -- B1.1 froze the `input` rule and const and add were left implicit -- so const(n) lowering to church(n+1) would have contradicted no sentence. An identity that cannot move when its map changes is the same defect as one that moves when its map has not. AND THE REFUSAL VOCABULARIES WERE CROSSED: the executable encoding listed four lower-* source-fragment refusals that cannot arise while emitting, while lowering claimed emit-unbound-port and template-malformed, neither reachable from lower(), which emits only zero-port templates it built itself. Each list now belongs to the record that owns it, and every name lowering claims is driven to a refusal by the witness. BUILT AT B2, AND BUILDING IT MOVED NEITHER SEMANTIC ID -- the property B1.1 split the records to make possible and the first round able to exercise it. `input` lowers to a structural port, instantiate() closes a template against canonical inputs, both lifecycle flags are true and all three port falsifiers are WITNESSED; none of that moved lsem or isem, and the measurement is an EQUATION rather than a simulation: put back only op_lowering_rules and only emission and the B1.2.1 identities return EXACTLY, so those two fields are the only hashed bytes the round touched. THE SOURCE-TO-TEMPLATE MAP IS STRUCTURAL AND INTERPRETED: lower() reads op_lowering_rules rather than carrying a second hand-coded copy of it, so a rule cannot be edited without changing behaviour and behaviour cannot change without moving LOWERING_SEM_ID. English rules beside a hand-coded implementation are two artifacts that can disagree while only one is hashed -- the codomain-in-prose defect one layer in -- and `transform: identity` on the port's source name is the no-normalization ruling made structural rather than stated. LOWER() NO LONGER RETURNS AN EXECUTABLE TERM. The convenience field was a SECOND PATH: the official route through instantiate() beside a shortcut through lowering, with every future reader having to remember which carried the semantics, which is how a hidden second mechanism returns. It is removed and the equality survives as a REGRESSION THEOREM -- instantiate(template, {}) reproduces the exact 129 bytes, the same six-frame film, the same normal form and the same 5. AND instantiate() MAY NOT MINT THE IDENTITY OF ITS OWN OUTPUT: an instantiator that emitted bytes and certified their semantic id would produce the artifact and the certificate from one source, so a wrong emission would carry a matching id and verify against itself. The kernel canonicalises the bytes; the receipt is built around that id; verification RE-INSTANTIATES and RE-CANONICALISES independently rather than asking the instantiator to agree with itself. THE EMISSION SPLIT TRIGGER MOVED TO STATUS and gained two conditions: split emission into its own relation when it becomes independently REUSED, independently THEOREM-BEARING, independently VERSIONED OR REPLACEABLE, or when the closed-template intermediate becomes an independently IDENTIFIED or EXTERNALLY OBSERVED artifact. The last two fire first -- the moment two emitters are compared over one closed template, an emitter upgrade re-cutting the semantic identity of PORT SUBSTITUTION is plainly wrong. Keeping that trigger inside the hashed semantics, as B1.2.1 did, re-committed B1.1's own finding: governance prose inside a relation identity re-identifies the relation when it is reworded. STILL DECLARED OPEN: source-refusal to instantiation-refusal preservation, unchanged.
